chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Abdullah ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said regarding slaughtering with something other than iron: If you are compelled to do so, and you do not find iron, then slaughter it with a stone. The meaning in these narrations is that we restrict it to the state of compulsion in which one is unable to find iron. As for when iron is available, slaughtering is not permissible in any case except with it.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to slaughter an animal with a stone if no knife is available?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) clarifies that while iron is the standard instrument for slaughter, non-iron tools are permissible in cases of absolute necessity (darurah) when iron is unavailable. This ruling distinguishes between the ideal requirement and the practical exception, ensuring the validity of the act even when the primary tool is absent, a principle consistent with Shia juristic methodology regarding flexibility in ritual purity and consumption.
